gloss: fire; an offering to the altar's fire
summary: אֵשׁ is fire: the fire that cooks, warms, refines and destroys, the fire kept burning on the altar day and night, and the fire in which Yahweh appeared at Sinai and by which he judged (Lev 6:6; Deu 4:12; Gen 19:24); Yahweh himself is “a consuming fire” (Deu 4:24). אִשֶּׁה is formed from it: what is given to the altar's fire, the offering or the part of it made to smoke there as “a scent of appeasement to Yahweh”, and from there the holy offerings as a whole, from which the priests ate their portion (Lev 2:2–3; 23:13, 37; Deu 18:1). Its doubled ש is the doubled ש of אֵשׁ with a suffix, אִשּׁוֹ “his fire” (Deu 4:36), and the Biblical Aramaic אֶשָּׁא, Ugaritic išt, Akkadian išātu and Phoenician ʾš are the same word for fire.

words.summary: Fire, in some 380 uses: in the hearth and the furnace, on the altar, in Yahweh's appearing and judgments, and in figures of his anger, his word and his refining. Before a vowel ending its ש is doubled, אִשּׁוֹ, אִשָּׁם (Deu 4:36; Isa 66:24), as in אִשֶּׁה.

senses.definition: Fire as people kindle and use it: carried with the wood for a burnt offering, lit to warm and to roast, fed by wood and dying without it, breaking out in a field, refining metal; and fire as the means of destroying a thing utterly, burning it “with fire”.

evidence.note: Abraham takes in his hand “the fire and the knife”.
“Here are the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?”
“Where there is no wood, the fire goes out (תִּכְבֶּה).”
“If fire breaks out and catches in thorns” and eats up the standing grain, the one who kindled it repays.
Half the wood he burns in the fire, roasts meat and warms himself: “I have seen the fire.”
The Passover lamb not raw nor boiled in water, but צְלִי־אֵשׁ, roasted with fire.
“You shall kindle no fire in any of your dwellings on the day of the שַׁבָּת.”
Whatever can come into the fire is passed through the fire and is clean; whatever cannot is passed through water.
Silver, bronze, iron, lead and tin gathered into a furnace “to blow fire on it, to melt it”.
Among the four never satisfied: “fire, which never says ‘Enough’.”
Moses burns the calf “with fire” and grinds it to powder.
Their carved images “you shall burn with fire”.
The one taken with the devoted thing “shall be burnt with fire, he and all he has”.

senses.definition: The fire laid on the altar and in the censers, which consumed the offerings and was never to go out; it was first kindled by fire that came out from before Yahweh, and any other fire offered before him was “strange fire”.

evidence.note: “אֵשׁ תָּמִיד, a continual fire, shall be kept burning on the altar; it shall not go out.”
“The fire on the altar shall burn on it”; the priest feeds it with wood every morning and lays the burnt offering on it.
The burnt offering on the hearth all night, “and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning in it”.
The sons of Aaron put fire on the altar and lay wood on the fire.
The fat made to smoke “on the wood that is on the fire, אִשֵּׁה, a scent of appeasement”: the fire and what is given to it side by side.
“Fire came out from before Yahweh and consumed the burnt offering and the fat on the altar”, and the people fell on their faces.
On the Day of Coverings the high priest takes a censer full of coals of fire from the altar before Yahweh.
Nadab and Abihu put fire in their censers and offered “אֵשׁ זָרָה, strange fire, which he had not commanded them”.
At Carmel “the fire of Yahweh fell and consumed the burnt offering, the wood, the stones and the dust”.
Yahweh answered David “with fire from the heavens on the altar of burnt offering”.
At the dedication of Solomon's house fire came down and consumed the offerings.

senses.gloss: fire as Yahweh's presence and judgment
senses.definition: Fire in which Yahweh showed himself (the bush, the pillar, Sinai) and fire he sent down in judgment, consuming those who rebelled; lightning is called fire from the heavens.

evidence.note: The messenger of Yahweh appeared “in a flame of fire” from the bush: “the bush was burning with fire, and the bush was not consumed”.
Yahweh went before them by night “in a pillar of fire, to give them light”.
Sinai smoked, “because Yahweh had come down on it in fire”.
“Yahweh spoke to you out of the midst of the fire; you heard the sound of words, but saw no form.”
“On earth he made you see אִשּׁוֹ הַגְּדוֹלָה, his great fire, and you heard his words out of the midst of the fire.”
“Yahweh rained on Sodom and on Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahweh out of the heavens.”
“Fire came out from before Yahweh and consumed them, and they died before Yahweh.”
At Taberah “the fire of Yahweh burned among them” when they complained.
Fire from Yahweh consumed the 250 men offering incense.
“If I am a man of God, let fire come down from the heavens and consume you and your fifty.”
“A chariot of fire and horses of fire” part Elijah and Elisha.
Hail “and fire flashing continually in the midst of the hail”: lightning.
“The fire of God fell from the heavens and burned up the sheep.”
Hailstones and coals of fire before him.
He makes “his ministers a flaming fire”.
The likeness above the throne had “the appearance of fire” round about.
“Behold, Yahweh will come with fire … to render his anger with fury and his rebuke with flames of fire.”
“By fire and by his sword Yahweh will judge all flesh.”
“I will send a fire on the house of Hazael, and it shall devour the palaces of Ben-hadad”: the refrain of Amos 1–2.
“I will be to her a wall of fire round about”: fire that guards Jerusalem.

senses.definition: Fire as a figure for what consumes, compels or purifies: Yahweh's jealousy and anger, his word in the prophet, passion and lust, the fire of trial through which he refines his people.

evidence.note: “Yahweh your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.”
He goes over before you “as a consuming fire”, to destroy the nations.
“Who among us shall dwell with the consuming fire?”
“The light of Israel shall be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame.”
“A fire is kindled in my anger, and it burns to the lowest grave.”
“Lest my fury go out like fire and burn, with none to quench it.”
“He poured out his fury like fire.”
“His fury is poured out like fire.”
“Is not my word like fire, says Yahweh, and like a hammer that breaks the rock?”
His word was “in my heart like a burning fire shut up in my bones”.
“While I mused the fire burned; then I spoke with my tongue.”
Love's flashes are “flashes of fire, a very flame of Yah”.
“Can a man take fire in his bosom and his clothes not be burned?” of going in to a neighbour's wife.
The worthless man: “on his lips is like a scorching fire”.
“I will bring the third part through the fire, and refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested; they shall call on my name.”
“He is like a refiner's fire.”
Joshua the high priest, “a brand plucked from the fire”.
“We went through fire and through water, and you brought us out to abundance.”
“When you walk through fire you shall not be burned.”

evidence.locator: Deu.4.24, אֵשׁ → πῦρ; Isa.66.24, אִשָּׁם → πῦρ; πῦρ renders אֵשׁ ×334

evidence.note: “Our God is a consuming fire”, from Deu 4:24.
“Where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched”, from Isa 66:24.
“His ministers a flame of fire”, from Psa 104:4.
“Blood and fire and vapour of smoke”, from Joel 3:3.
The messenger “in a flame of fire in a bush”, from Exo 3:2.
“Shall we command fire to come down from heaven and consume them, as Elijah did?”, from 2Ki 1:10.
On the day Lot went out of Sodom “it rained fire and brimstone from heaven”, from Gen 19:24.
Not to the mountain that “burned with fire”, from Deu 4:11.
Faith tested by fire like gold, as in Zec 13:9.

parallels.note: Flame, the fire's tongue, set beside it.
Brimstone, with fire in Yahweh's overthrow of the wicked.
Smoke, which fire makes: at Sinai and among the signs of Yahweh's day.

opposites.note: Water, the other ordeal and the other cleansing: what cannot pass through fire passes through water.

phrases.gloss: strange fire, fire Yahweh did not command
make (a child) pass through the fire, to Molech

evidence.note: Topheth “in the valley of the son of Hinnom”, where a man made his son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech.

words.summary: What is given to Yahweh's altar fire: 65 uses, all in the law of offerings (Exodus to Numbers), with Deu 18:1, Jos 13:14 and 1Sa 2:28. It is tied to the fire by its form (the doubled ש of אִשּׁוֹ, “his fire”), by the verb that goes with it, הִקְטִיר “make to smoke” on the altar, and by the text setting it beside אֵשׁ (Lev 3:5). It also covers what was brought with the burnt part and not itself burned (the drink offering, Num 15:10) and the holy offerings from which the priests ate, so that some read it as “gift”; scripture's use fits “what is given to the fire”, the whole offering named from its altar part.

senses.gloss: an offering made to smoke on the altar
senses.definition: An offering, or the part of it, burned on the altar to Yahweh: the whole burnt offering, the fat of the peace offering, the memorial handful of the grain offering, the frankincense on the bread of the presence. It is “a scent of appeasement to Yahweh” and called his food.

evidence.note: “The priest shall make all of it smoke on the altar: a burnt offering, אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ־נִיחוֹחַ, a fire-offering, a scent of appeasement to Yahweh.”
Made to smoke “on the wood that is on the fire, אִשֵּׁה”.
The priest takes a handful of the grain offering and makes its memorial part smoke on the altar, “אִשֵּׁה, a scent of appeasement”.
“No leaven and no honey shall you make smoke from it as אִשֶּׁה to Yahweh”: what is made to smoke is the אִשֶּׁה.
“The priest shall make it smoke on the altar, לֶחֶם אִשֶּׁה, the food of the fire-offering to Yahweh.”
Pure frankincense on each row of the bread, “for a memorial, אִשֶּׁה to Yahweh”: the frankincense is burned, the bread eaten (Lev 24:9).
The ram of consecration: “a burnt offering to Yahweh, a scent of appeasement, an אִשֶּׁה to Yahweh”.
The priests wash before they come near the altar “to make an אִשֶּׁה smoke to Yahweh”.
Whoever eats the fat of a beast “from which an אִשֶּׁה is offered to Yahweh” is cut off.
The priests offer “the אִשֵּׁי of Yahweh, the bread of their God”.
From the eighth day an ox, sheep or goat is accepted “for an offering, an אִשֶּׁה to Yahweh”.
“My offering, my food for my fire-offerings (לְאִשַּׁי), my scent of appeasement, you shall keep to offer to me at its appointed time.”
Wine for the drink offering, half a hin, “אִשֵּׁה, a scent of appeasement”: the drink offering counted with the burnt offering it went with.
The firstborn of ox, sheep and goat: their blood thrown on the altar, their fat made to smoke as an אִשֶּׁה.

senses.gloss: the fire-offering of the appointed times
senses.definition: In Leviticus 23 and Numbers 28–29, “you shall bring near an אִשֶּׁה to Yahweh” is the standing command for each מוֹעֵד: the burnt, grain and drink offerings and sacrifices appointed for its day.

evidence.note: “These are Yahweh's appointed times … to bring near an אִשֶּׁה to Yahweh: burnt offering and grain offering, sacrifice and drink offerings, each day's matter on its day.”
Seven days of מַצּוֹת: “you shall bring near an אִשֶּׁה to Yahweh seven days”.
With the עֹמֶר's lamb, two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, “an אִשֶּׁה to Yahweh, a scent of appeasement”.
With the bread of the fiftieth day: the burnt offerings “with their grain offering and their drink offerings, an אִשֵּׁה, a scent of appeasement”.
The first of the seventh month.
The Day of Coverings.
Seven days of סֻכּוֹת and the eighth day.
The continual burnt offering, two lambs a day.

senses.gloss: the fire-offerings of Yahweh, as the priests' portion
senses.definition: In the plural, אִשֵּׁי יַהְוֶה, the holy offerings as a whole, of which part was burned and part given to the priests to eat: the Levites' inheritance in place of land.

evidence.note: “What is left of the grain offering is Aaron's and his sons': a most holy thing מֵאִשֵּׁי יַהְוֶה, from Yahweh's fire-offerings”, after the handful was burned (Lev 2:2).
Every male of Aaron's sons shall eat it, “a lasting due … from Yahweh's fire-offerings”.
“This is the anointing portion of Aaron and of his sons from Yahweh's fire-offerings.”
Eat it in a holy place, “for it is your due and your sons' due from Yahweh's fire-offerings”.
The bread of the presence is Aaron's, “most holy to him from Yahweh's fire-offerings”.
The Levites have no portion with Israel: “they shall eat the אִשֵּׁי of Yahweh and his inheritance”.
To Levi he gave no inheritance: “the אִשֵּׁי of Yahweh, the God of Israel, are his inheritance”.
“I gave to the house of your father all the אִשֵּׁי of the sons of Israel.”

evidence.locator: Lev.23.13, אִשֶּׁה לַיהוה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ → θυσία τῷ κυρίῳ ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας; θυσία renders אִשֶּׁה ×8

evidence.note: Christ “gave himself for us, an offering and a θυσία to God for a scent of sweet smell (εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας)”: the words of אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ.
The Philippians' gift: “a scent of sweet smell, a θυσία acceptable, well-pleasing to God”.

parallels.note: The burnt offering, wholly burned: the אִשֶּׁה par excellence.
What is brought near: Yahweh's offering, his food for his fire-offerings.
Food: the fire-offering is called Yahweh's food, the bread of God.

phrases.gloss: a fire-offering, a scent of appeasement to Yahweh
bring near a fire-offering to Yahweh
Yahweh's fire-offerings (the priests' and Levites' portion)

words.summary: A feminine form of אֵשׁ, read in the written text of Jer 6:29, where the consonants מאשתם give מֵאֶשָּׁתָם “from their fire”; the reading tradition divides them מֵאֵשׁ תַּם, “by the fire the lead is consumed”, which is the text counted here. Its form is the form of Aramaic אֶשָּׁא, Ugaritic išt and Akkadian išātu.

senses.definition: The bellows blow, the fire refines in vain: the wicked are not separated out.

evidence.note: “The bellows blow; the lead is consumed of the fire (written מאשתם); in vain the refiner refines.”

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic for fire, once, in Daniel's vision of the beast slain and given to the burning; elsewhere Daniel's Aramaic says נוּר.

senses.definition: The fire into which the fourth beast's body is given after it is slain: its destruction.

evidence.note: “I watched until the beast was slain and its body destroyed and given לִיקֵדַת אֶשָּׁא, to the burning of fire.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's word of this root is not fire, for which it says ܢܘܪܐ, but fever, the fire in the body, where the Greek has πυρετός, itself named from πῦρ. Jewish Aramaic אֶשָּׁא has both senses, fire and fever, and Akkadian išātu is also inflammation.

senses.definition: A burning fever, which Jesus rebukes and which leaves the sick at his word.

evidence.note: Peter's wife's mother lying sick with fever.
He touched her hand and the fever left her.
He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her.
“Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.”
Publius' father sick with fever and dysentery.

cognates.note: Feminine in -t, as Aramaic אֶשָּׁא and Akkadian išātu; written syllabically i-ša-ti, /ʾišat-/. Ugaritic keeps š and ṯ apart, and has š: the older sound behind the root's ש.

evidence.note: “išt ‘fire’ (H. ʾēš, Jew.-Aram. ʾiššāṯā, Akkad. išātu)”.

evidence.locator: p. 40, §43.1, Patterns with fewer than three consonants
evidence.note: f. /ʾišat-/, alphabetic išt, syllabic i-ša-ti “fire”.

cognates.note: Its senses run as the Hebrew's and the Syriac's do: fire, lightning (fire from the heavens, Exo 9:24), and inflammation (the Peshitta's fever).

evidence.note: Meanings “fire; inflammation; lightning”, 1,940 instances.

cognates.note: In Kilamuwa's inscription the king was among stronger kings “like a fire that consumes the beard and like a fire that consumes the hand”: fire that eats, as אֵשׁ אֹכְלָה.

evidence.note: “n.f. FIRE”; KAI 24.5–6 (Ph) km ʾš ʾklt zqn w[km] ʾš ʾklt yd.

cognates.note: The Targum's word for fire (Targ. Gen 15:17) and, in the Talmud, for fever: both senses of the root in one word.

evidence.note: “1) fire. Targ. Gen. XV, 17; a. fr. … 2) fever. Targ. Y. Gen. XXI, 15.—Yoma 29ᵃ אישתא וכ׳ the fever in winter time.”

cognates.note: Fisher sets Ugaritic išt beside the Ethiopic word for fire in Geʿez, Tigre and Amharic. Read from the OCR text only, which garbles the Ethiopic form; the page image is not checked.

evidence.note: OCR: “išt fire Gz, Te, Am … fire”.

doctrine.statement: Israel heard Yahweh's voice “out of the midst of the fire” and saw no form (Deu 4:12, 36), and Moses told them why they must make no image: “Yahweh your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God” (Deu 4:24). The fire that came out from before him accepted the first offerings on the altar (Lev 9:24) and, in the next breath, consumed Nadab and Abihu for offering fire he had not commanded (Lev 10:1–2). Hebrews takes Moses' words to the ecclesia: having come not to the mountain that burned with fire but to mount Zion, “let us serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear, for our God is a consuming fire” (Heb 12:18–29). From the verses: the same fire accepts what is offered as he commands and destroys what is offered otherwise; his worship is on his terms, and his holiness is no less now than at Sinai.

Isaiah ends with the worshippers going out to “look on the carcasses (פִּגְרֵי) of the men who transgressed against me, for their worm shall not die and their fire (אִשָּׁם) shall not be quenched” (Isa 66:24): what the fire and worm work on are dead bodies, looked at by the living. “Shall not be quenched” is said of the altar's fire, which was never let go out (Lev 6:6), and of the fire Yahweh would kindle in Jerusalem's gates, which “shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem and shall not be quenched” (Jer 17:27): fire no one puts out, which burns until it has consumed what it was set to, not fire that burns for ever. Jesus quotes Isa 66:24 of γέεννα, the valley of Hinnom (Mrk 9:43–48), where Israel had burned their sons and daughters in the fire, “which I did not command, nor did it come into my heart” (Jer 7:31; 2Ki 23:10), and which Jeremiah said would become a valley of slaughter where the dead are buried (Jer 7:32). Sodom and Gomorrah, set forth as an example “suffering the vengeance of eternal fire” (Jud 1:7), were overthrown by fire from Yahweh (Gen 19:24–25) and turned to ashes (2Pe 2:6). From the verses: the fire of judgment destroys; it does not keep the wicked alive in it.

What was given to Yahweh's altar fire was “an אִשֶּׁה, a scent of appeasement to Yahweh” (Lev 1:9), and at each appointed time Israel was to bring near an אִשֶּׁה (Lev 23:37). Paul uses those words of Christ: he “loved us and gave himself for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for a scent of sweet smell” (Eph 5:2), the Septuagint's θυσία … ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας for אִשֶּׁה … רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ (Lev 23:13); and of the gifts of believers, “a scent of sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, well-pleasing to God” (Php 4:18). From the verses: the offerings given to the fire at the feasts showed in figure the giving up of a life to God that he accepts, which Christ gave, and which those who walk in love give after him.

Yahweh brings “the third part through the fire” to refine them as silver and test them as gold, and they call on his name (Zec 13:9); the messenger of the covenant comes “like a refiner's fire” to purify the sons of Levi (Mal 3:2–3); Israel came “through fire and through water” to abundance (Psa 66:12). Peter uses the figure of the trial of faith, “much more precious than gold that perishes, though it is tested by fire” (1Pe 1:7), and Paul of each one's work, which “the day will declare, because it is revealed by fire” (1Co 3:13). From the verses: fire that destroys the wicked is the same fire that proves and purifies those who are his.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Leviticus 23 (אִשֶּׁה, Lev 23:8, 13, 18, 25, 27, 36, 37). Root key: the database keys אִשֶּׁה (a.gb.ac) and the Kethiv אֶשָּׁה (a.gb.ab) under אשה, and gives אֵשׁ (a.gb.aa) no root at all (its 378 tokens carry an empty morphology root), so the entry takes אשה, the key the corpus uses. אֵשׁ is given no word `root`: its own consonants would be אש, which the corpus uses for Biblical Aramaic אֹשׁ “foundation” (xa.bi.ai, Ezr 4:12; 5:16; 6:3), and a word root אש would put this entry on those tokens; its tokens find the entry through a.gb.aa. Decision on אִשֶּׁה: kept with אֵשׁ. For: (1) the doubled ש, as in אֵשׁ with a suffix (אִשּׁוֹ Deu 4:36; Job 18:5; אִשָּׁם Isa 66:24) and in Aramaic אֶשָּׁא; (2) it goes with הִקְטִיר “make smoke” (Lev 1:9; 2:2, 11; 3:11) and is set beside הָאֵשׁ (Lev 1:17; 3:5); (3) Lev 2:11 defines it as what is made to smoke. Against: it also covers wine (Num 15:10) and what the priests eat (Lev 2:3; 24:9; Deu 18:1; Jos 13:14; 1Sa 2:28); this is read as the whole offering named from its burnt part. The English translation in the database renders it “gift”; a proposed Ugaritic cognate meaning “gift” (with ṯ, which would split the root) was looked for and not found in Segert's glossary (only un and itnn “gift”), so it is not entered; if found in DULAT it should be added as `possible` with sounds {ש: ṯ}. Left out, from BDB's grouping under the same key אשה (a.gd.*), as words of other roots: אָשְׁיָה “buttress, foundation” (a.gd.ab, Jer 50:15, 0 tokens), which with Aramaic אֹשׁ “foundation” and Akkadian uššu “foundation” (Oracc armep x000038920) belongs to a root ʾšš/ʾšy “found”, a homograph that wants its own entry; אֶשֶׁךְ “testicle” (a.gd.ak, Lev 21:20; Akkadian iškum, Ugaritic ušk: a root ʾšk); אֶשְׁכּוֹל “cluster” (a.gd.al; Ugaritic uṯkl); the names יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ Josiah (a.gd.ac, j.af.ab), אֶשְׁכֹּל Eshcol (a.gd.am), אַשְׁכְּנַז Ashkenaz (a.gd.an), אֲשִׁימָא Ashima (a.gd.aj); and the place and people names אַשּׁוּר Asshur/Assyria (a.gd.af, from Akkadian Aššur), אַשּׁוּרִם (a.gd.ag), אֲשׁוּרִי (a.gd.ah). Because the morphology gives all of these the root אשה, the app's root lookup will show this entry on their tokens (291) until they have entries of their own. Also not this word: a.gb.ad אִשׁ “there is” (2Sa 14:19; Mic 6:10), a by-form of יֵשׁ. Greek: Thayer's “Hebr. אֵשׁ” under πῦρ is an equivalence, not a derivation, so πῦρ is a rendering, not a loan. Peshitta: SEDRA root 229 ܐܫ, lexeme 309 ܐܫܬܐ “fever” (verses from the BFBS word list); the Peshitta's fire is ܢܘܪܐ. Arabic has no word for fire of this root (Lane's أُسّ is “foundation”). Not consulted: Dillmann and Leslau for Geʿez (Fisher read by OCR only, p. 49 by the OCR's page number), DULAT, CAD išātu. Open questions for review: (1) whether אִשֶּׁה should be glossed “fire-offering” (as here) or “offering, gift”; (2) the entry root אשה, shared by the BDB group above; (3) whether a ʾšš “foundation” entry (Aramaic אֹשׁ, Hebrew אָשְׁיָה) should be made as homograph 2 of אשה; (4) the unquenched-fire doctrine.
